doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Dance marathons
summary: Ware describes dance marathons where Erskine Tate's band played on for weeks while contestants danced for prizes.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Because I remember Erskine Tate was working down at one of those dance marathons -- what was the name of that club down on Wabash -- we'd stop by there and try to play; kind of spare the musicians a little bit -- a lot of people was dancing for these prizes. You know what I mean by a dance marathon? Dance for weeks.
Uh huh. Well, that band has got to play right along.
And this was in the thirties?
People would dance until they fell out.
Well, for a prize of $1,000 -- a thousand dollars was a whole lot of money. You know.
But like I said, there was a whole lot of music out there ... beautiful music.
